osmTags.inscription:
William Wallinger M.A. was the first incumbent of St. Mary in-the-Castle, Hastings.

Beyond this spot was once the plantation - a beautifully landscaped garden with an abudance of trees and flora, adorned with orchards and a parterre. A meandering pathway

George Street, pedestrian shopping street.
The street was formally re-opened by Bernard Bresslaw on April 25th 1987

MURIEL MATTERS-PORTER
1877-1969
Adelaide born activist
First woman to 'speak' in the House of Commons
Lived in this house
1949-1969
George Devey 1820‒1886, architect and pioneer of the Arts & Crafts Movement, lived in this house 1870‒1886
Arthur Haygarth, cricketer, historian, Old Harrovian, was born here on 4th August 1825
Lewis Carroll (1832‒1898), writer and scholar, was a frequent visitor to this house, the home of his aunts the Misses Lutwidge

eras.label: Mapped site · auto T1
eras.summary: Mapped outline, terrain and present-day surroundings from open data. No historic reconstruction.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.
